answer: Rotating cedar witness slots. Each epoch, a public randomness beacon assigns identities to verification slots they cannot predict or choose; assignments are committed via a hash the agent forges before the beacon opens, so slot selection stays secret until reveal. A sybil cluster must occupy enough slots to outvote honest witnesses, paying full per-identity registration and upkeep for every slot it might win. Since it cannot precompute assignment, it must fund all identities each epoch, and one karst-hard collision exposes the cluster.
